MSI2 fixed-peak CLIP analysis | Peak counting, paired DESeq2, construct comparison, and transcript-region exploration | Eight libraries | Two matched IP/input pairs per construct | Analysis summary | September 2026

REPRODUCIBILITY | Matched-pair ratios agree only weakly across replicates | 328WT: Pearson r = 0.188, Spearman rho = 0.164 | 324WT: Pearson r = 0.160, Spearman rho = 0.192 | All 493 enriched 328WT peaks and 142 of 144 enriched 324WT peaks have positive enrichment in both pairs.

PEAK-LEVEL VIEWS | Representative peaks confirm paired IP enrichment | Heatmaps retain individual samples, show log2(normalized count + 0.5), and z-score within each selected peak. Up to 75 reproducibly enriched peaks were selected per construct.
CONSTRUCT COMPARISON | Separate DESeq2 effects are moderately concordant where both models test the peak | 1,095 | peaks tested in both separate models | Pearson r = 0.413 | Spearman rho = 0.421

PEAK AND GENE IDENTITY | Peak overlap is larger than gene overlap alone suggests | Measure | 328WT | 324WT | Shared | Significantly enriched peaks | 493 | 144 | 86 | Unique Ensembl gene IDs | 419 | 127 | 82 | Protein-coding among significant-associated IDs | 93.3% | 93.7% | n/a | 324WT-only enriched peaks | 58 | enriched in 324WT but not 328WT | 14 | were not tested in 328WT; all associated gene IDs map as protein-coding | The remaining 44 were tested in 328WT but did not meet adjusted significance there. | A peak may carry more than one gene ID when overlapping same-strand source peaks came from different transcript annotations. | Significance in one construct and not the other remains a descriptive category.

PEAK PROVENANCE | Why MSI2_peak_036101 contains two gene IDs | Merged peak | MSI2_peak_036101 | chr16:18,791,950-18,792,150 | minus strand | Contributing source peak | Gene ID | Score | Coordinates | ENSG00000260342.2_47782 | ENSG00000260342 | 31.68 | 18,791,950-18,792,150 | ENSG00000170540.14_47786 | ENSG00000170540 | 25.30 | 18,791,981-18,792,150 | Both original omniCLIP rows overlap on the same strand, so peak preparation merged them into one fixed region and retained both source gene IDs for provenance. | The two IDs do not mean the count was assigned twice; featureCounts counted the merged interval once. | The representative summit comes from the highest-scoring source peak and supports the transcript-region annotation. | This peak is significantly enriched in both constructs: DESeq2 log2FC 4.67 in 328WT and 2.98 in 324WT.
VALIDATION | Original omniCLIP score predicts new enrichment only weakly | 328WT Spearman rho = 0.189 | 324WT Spearman rho = 0.169

ALL 16,046 PEAKS | Pseudocount-normalized ratios extend the construct comparison to all countable peaks | Per construct | log2((mean CLIP CPM + 0.5) / | (mean SMI CPM + 0.5)) | 0.143 | Pearson correlation across all 16,046 countable peaks | Replicates are averaged within CLIP and SMI before calculating the ratio. | The pseudocount keeps zero-count combinations finite. | Horizontal and vertical bands reflect zero or very low counts and require caution.

REGION ANALYSIS | Transcript-region annotation and background choices | Annotation rule | Represent each merged peak by the summit of its highest-scoring source peak. | Annotate strand-specifically against TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene. | Collapse to 5' UTR, CDS, 3' UTR, intron, and Other. | Cache one transcript-region assignment per merged peak for reuse. | Region | 43,794 merged | 46,108 source | 16,046 counted | 5' UTR | 0.36% | 0.37% | 0.39% | CDS | 4.18% | 4.18% | 6.38% | 3' UTR | 59.91% | 59.86% | 81.78% | Intron | 29.38% | 29.38% | 5.82% | Other | 6.17% | 6.21% | 5.64% | Primary background | All 43,794 merged peaks use the same unit as the selected merged peaks. | Sensitivity background | All 46,108 score-filtered source peaks provide nearly identical expected region proportions.

EXPLORATORY SELECTION | Construct-preference definitions became progressively less restrictive | Strict opposite quadrants: 224 peaks favor 324WT and 3,024 favor 328WT. | Delta groups: 1,437 favor 324WT, 7,034 favor 328WT, and 717 are similar-positive.

REGION ENRICHMENT | Selected delta groups concentrate in 3' UTRs relative to the complete peak landscape | Tests against background | Overall merged-background test: 2 by 5 Pearson chi-square with a Monte Carlo p-value from 100,000 replicates. | Per-region merged-background tests: two-sided Fisher exact tests with BH adjustment across five regions. | Source-background sensitivity: chi-square goodness-of-fit plus exact binomial tests with BH adjustment. | Against 43,794 merged peaks | 324-biased: 84.20% 3' UTR, 1.405-fold | 328-biased: 88.90% 3' UTR, 1.484-fold | Similar-positive: 91.21% 3' UTR, 1.522-fold | Selection requires measurable CLIP/SMI signal, so direct construct comparisons are more informative than selected-versus-background effects alone.

OVERVIEW | Analysis progression | 01 | Count a fixed peak universe | Preserve original omniCLIP peaks while measuring all eight libraries on the same coordinates. | 02 | Estimate enrichment within each construct | Run paired IP versus input models separately for 328WT and 324WT. | 03 | Inspect abundance, replicates, and sample structure | Use PCA, heatmaps, MA plots, pair ratios, and representative peaks. | 04 | Compare constructs descriptively | Compare effect sizes, significant-peak overlap, shared genes, and original peak scores. | 05 | Ask where construct-biased peaks occur | Annotate summits to transcript regions and compare selected groups with complete peak backgrounds. | 06 | Return to a continuous preference measure | Filter out peaks depleted in both constructs, then plot delta-delta across transcript regions.

DIRECT REGION COMPARISON | 324-biased and 328-biased peaks differ significantly, but the global effect is small | 36.72 | Pearson chi-square, 4 degrees of freedom | <1e-5 | Monte Carlo p-value with 100,000 replicates | 0.066 | Cramer's V | Region | 324-biased | 328-biased | 324/328 fold | BH-adjusted p | 3' UTR | 84.20% | 88.90% | 0.947 | 6.44e-6 | CDS | 6.26% | 4.02% | 1.557 | 5.06e-4 | Intron | 5.08% | 2.80% | 1.814 | 5.76e-5 | 5' UTR | 0.42% | 0.28% | 1.468 | 0.537 | Other | 4.04% | 3.99% | 1.010 | 0.941 | The direct comparison supports a modest shift: 324-biased peaks contain relatively more CDS and intron assignments and relatively fewer 3' UTR assignments.

FINAL EXPLORATORY VIEW | Continuous delta-delta after the relaxed positive-preferred filter | Retain a peak when | delta >= 0 and 324WT LFC > 0 | or | delta <= 0 and 328WT LFC > 0 | 9,369 | retained peaks | -3.859 | overall median delta-delta | Delta-delta stays continuous; the rule only filters peaks depleted relative to SMI in both constructs. | 7,571 retained peaks have negative delta and 1,798 have positive delta. | All five region-specific paired Wilcoxon tests remain significant after BH correction.

SUMMARY | Interpretation and next statistical step | What the current analysis supports | Both constructs show clear IP enrichment at reproducible peak subsets. | The 328WT libraries yield more countable and significant peaks than 324WT. | Most enriched peaks localize to 3' UTRs, and direct region differences between delta groups are statistically convincing but small. | The relaxed continuous delta view is strongly shifted toward 328WT, consistent with the library imbalance. | Limits | Only two biological pairs per construct leave one residual degree of freedom in each paired model. | Pseudocount ratios are sensitive to zero and low counts. | A significant peak in one construct and a nonsignificant peak in the other does not test the construct difference. | Formal follow-up | Fit a combined count model with a construct-by-assay interaction. The interaction term directly tests whether the IP/input effect differs between 324WT and 328WT.

INPUTS | Experimental design and fixed peak universe | Construct | Pair A IP | Pair A input | Pair B IP | Pair B input | 328WT | 0081 | 0082 | 0083 | 0084 | 324WT | 0085 | 0086 | 0087 | 0088 | 58,555 | original omniCLIP BED rows | 46,108 | source peaks with score at least 1 | 43,794 | same-strand merged peak regions | featureCounts measured every library against the same merged regions. | Raw integer counts feed DESeq2. Full mapped-library totals define size factors. | The BAMs remain on Bodhi, so this repository stores the downloaded count and model outputs.

FILTERING AND MODEL | Why only 2,769 and 1,546 peaks entered DESeq2 | 16,046 | merged peaks with any count across all eight libraries | 2,769 | 328WT peaks with total count at least 10 across its four samples | 1,546 | 324WT peaks with total count at least 10 across its four samples | Paired model | design = ~ pair + assay | DESeq2 compared IP with input separately within 328WT and 324WT. | Positive log2 fold change means IP enrichment. | The Wald test produced p-values; Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment controlled FDR at 0.05. | DESeq2 independent filtering left 1,320 nonmissing adjusted p-values for 328WT and 377 for 324WT. | The 16,046-peak PCA and heatmap use all peaks with any count. They do not inherit the construct-specific DESeq2 count filter.

SAMPLE QC | Library depth and fixed-peak assignment | IP libraries consistently place a larger fraction of reads in fixed peaks | 328WT IP: 22.78% and 22.80% assigned. | 328WT input: 5.22% and 4.71% assigned. | 324WT IP: 8.85% and 10.34% assigned. | 324WT input: 3.67% and 4.12% assigned. | 324WT IP libraries contain fewer fixed-peak counts than 328WT IP libraries.

SAMPLE QC | PCA and sample correlation reveal strong library structure | PCA and correlation used 4,385 peaks with total count at least 10 across all eight samples. IP and input separate, but replicate structure remains strong, especially for 324WT.

EXPANDED PEAK UNIVERSE | All 16,046 countable peaks retain the same broad sample separation | PC1 explains 30.44% and PC2 explains 19.15%. The heatmap uses VST values, row z-scores, and eight deterministic k-means clusters.
PAIRED DESEQ2 | Within-construct MA plots show many large positive effects | 328WT | 494 significant peaks | 493 enriched, 1 depleted | 324WT | 144 significant peaks | all 144 enriched

PAIRED DESEQ2 | Volcano plots emphasize effect size and adjusted significance | Horizontal reference: adjusted p = 0.05. Vertical references: absolute log2 fold change = 1. The effect-size lines guide interpretation; they do not define significance.
